details: Living organisms display all core biological traits simultaneously: nutrition, respiration, growth, response to stimuli, excretion, reproduction, lifespan.
Non-living objects may show isolated features (a moving car, a growing cloud) but lack cellular organization, metabolic self-repair, and biological reproduction.
Life is characterized by active internal cellular energy transformation and self-sustaining organization.
Biological movement originates internally, unlike mechanical motion caused by external forces or fuel combustion.

details: Nutrition: Consuming food for cellular energy, maintenance, and growth.
Respiration: Biochemical breakdown of digested food in cells to release energy (inhaling O2, exhaling CO2).
Growth: Irreversible internal increase in body size and cell number throughout life stages.
Response to Stimuli: Functional reaction to environmental changes (light, heat, touch, sound, chemical).
Excretion: Removal of toxic metabolic waste products from the body.
Reproduction: Producing new individual offspring of one's own species (via seeds, eggs, or live birth).
Lifespan: Natural finite life cycle starting at birth, growth, reproduction, aging, and death.

branches.theme: 10.3 Plant Movements & Sensitivity to External Stimuli

details: Plants display movement and sensitivity without locomotion.
Chhui-mui (Touch-me-not / Mimosa pudica): Exhibits rapid thigmonastic leaf folding and drooping when touched.
Phototropism: Plant shoots grow orientationally toward sunlight stimulus.
Gravitropism: Roots grow downward in response to gravity.
experiments_or_examples: Touching Chhui-mui leaves and watching them fold closed in seconds
Placing a potted plant near a window and observing stem bending toward sunlight

branches.theme: 10.4 Latent Life, Seed Dormancy, & Germination Requirements

details: Latent Life: Dry seeds in storage remain dormant with minimal metabolic rate.
Environmental Triggers: Water (hydration), Air (oxygen for respiration), and Suitable Warm Temperature break dormancy.
Germination: Seed absorbs water, seed coat splits, radicle grows into root, plumule grows into shoot seedling.
Warmth speeds up metabolic enzyme activity needed to break down stored seed nutrients.
